meta.review_notes: Privacy policy is a generic website template (mentions 'blog, website or app', 'surf the website', 'Google AdSense') with multiple contradictions regarding the app's actual child-directed nature.

app.name: Wingo - Daily Planner for Kids
app.developer: DREAM ORIENTED YAZILIM VE BILISIM LIMITED SIRKETI
app.description: A simplified daily calendar and visual planner app designed for kids, especially children with special needs and developmental disorders, to plan and track daily activities.

verdict.one_liner: A helpful planner app for children with special needs that mostly keeps data on-device, but its privacy policy is a generic website template with contradictions.
verdict.summary: Wingo helps children with special needs plan their day through visual timelines and activity tracking. The developer promises not to sell personal data and uses Apple for payments. However, the privacy policy is clearly a copy-paste website template that contradicts the app's actual child-directed purpose and leaves many details unclear.
verdict.recommendation_reason: The app has good intentions for children's privacy and does not engage in aggressive data collection, but parents should be aware the privacy documentation is weak and generic.

red.title: Privacy policy is a generic website template
red.plain_english: The privacy policy repeatedly mentions 'blog, website or app,' 'surf the website,' and 'Google AdSense' — things that have nothing to do with a kids' planner app. This suggests the developer copy-pasted a template without customizing it for this product.

red.title: Contradiction about collecting children's data
red.plain_english: The app is made for children with special needs, but the policy claims it does not collect information from children under 13. This directly contradicts the app's purpose and suggests the developer may not fully understand child privacy laws.

red.title: Allows third-party behavioral tracking
red.plain_english: The policy states that third-party behavioral tracking is allowed on their site, and non-personally identifiable visitor information may be provided to other parties for marketing and advertising.

green.title: Promises not to sell personal data
green.plain_english: The developer explicitly says they do not sell, trade, or transfer your personal information to outside parties unless they give you advance notice first.

green.title: No advertising currently in the app
green.plain_english: The developer says Google AdSense is not currently enabled and they do not monetize child-targeted products with ads. Any future ads would be human-reviewed for kid-suitability.

green.title: COPPA parental controls mentioned
green.plain_english: For apps made for kids, parents are prompted to allow or deny the collection of usability data. Parents can also contact the developer to review, delete, or manage their child's information.

green.title: Payments handled securely by Apple
green.plain_english: All subscription payments are processed through Apple, and the developer does not store or process your credit card information on their own servers.

green.title: Honors Do Not Track signals
green.plain_english: The developer says they honor Do Not Track browser signals and do not plant tracking cookies when a user has DNT enabled.

categories.plain_english: The app stores your activity cards and daily planner data on your device so you can organize your schedule.
categories.detail: The app is a daily planner that stores user-created activity timelines, planner boards, and activity cards locally on the device. No broad file system access is mentioned.

categories.label: Data Sharing with 3rd Parties
categories.plain_english: The developer says they do not sell your personal information, but they may share it with website hosting partners and other companies that help run their service. Non-personal visitor information may also be shared for marketing and advertising.
categories.detail: The policy states: 'We do not sell, trade, or otherwise transfer to outside parties your Personally Identifiable Information unless we provide users with advance notice. This does not include website hosting partners and other parties who assist us in operating our website, conducting our business, or serving our users, so long as those parties agree to keep this information confidential.' It also notes: 'non-personally identifiable visitor information may be provided to other parties for marketing, advertising, or other uses.'
categories.policy_excerpt: We do not sell, trade, or otherwise transfer to outside parties your Personally Identifiable Information unless we provide users with advance notice... non-personally identifiable visitor information may be provided to other parties for marketing, advertising, or other uses.

categories.label: Behavioural & Ad Tracking
categories.plain_english: The developer allows third-party behavioral tracking and says they may enable Google AdSense in the future. They do not currently use cookies for tracking.

It also mentions: 'We have not enabled Google AdSense on our site but we may do so in the future.' Additionally: 'We do not use cookies for tracking purposes.' Non-personally identifiable visitor information may be provided for marketing and advertising.

Potential future Google AdSense
Non-PII visitor data shared for marketing

categories.label: Children's Data Handling
categories.plain_english: The app is made for children with special needs, and the developer claims to follow COPPA rules. Parents can contact them to manage their child's data. However, the policy also claims they do not collect information from children under 13, which contradicts the app's purpose.
categories.detail: The app is explicitly designed for children, especially those with special needs and developmental disorders. The COPPA section states: 'We market to, but do not collect information from children under 13.' This is contradictory since the app requires registration and subscription. However, the policy also mentions parental consent prompts: 'For apps and websites we sustain made especially for kids, parents will be prompted with a conversation where they can explicitly allow or deny the collection of usability data from kids under 13.' Parents can review, delete, manage, or refuse data sharing by contacting the developer.
categories.policy_excerpt: We market to, but do not collect information from children under 13. We don't let third-parties, including ad networks or plug-ins collect PII from children under 13... For apps and websites we sustain made especially for kids, parents will be prompted with a conversation where they can explicitly allow or deny the collection of usability data from kids under 13.
concerns: Contradiction: app is for children but policy claims not to collect from under-13s
No explicit COPPA compliance certification

categories.detail: The policy explicitly states: 'All transactions are processed through a gateway provider and are not stored or processed on our servers.' Subscriptions are handled via Apple In-App Purchases.

categories.label: Data Deletion & User Rights
categories.plain_english: Parents can contact the developer to review, delete, or manage their child's information, but there is no automatic self-delete button in the app.
categories.detail: The COPPA section states: 'Parents can review, delete, manage or refuse with whom their child's information is shared through contacting us directly.' Users can also change personal information by logging into their account. No self-service data deletion or automated export is mentioned.
categories.policy_excerpt: Parents can review, delete, manage or refuse with whom their child's information is shared through contacting us directly... Can change your personal information: By logging in to your account
